statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks were judged across five representative paths. Search results, authenticated account areas, payment, upload/creator onboarding, and post-verification playback were not covered because they are separate templates or require account/identity state.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page application with bundled client-side enhancement
page.notes: Public adult-media catalogue localized to GB. UK legal age verification gates playback. Cookie consent appeared on every fresh browser profile.

paths.description: Public homepage and trending-video listing, representing the primary discovery surface.
Representative video-detail and watch journey, including the UK age-verification gate.
Account creation journey, including social/email choices, blank submission, autocomplete, privacy disclosure and mobile layout.
Deliberately invalid route, representing HTTP error and recovery handling.

findings.summary: The desktop canvas is forced into mobile viewports.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout primitive reports scrollWidth 1024, clientWidth 360 and 664 px horizontal overflow on both home and video detail; screenshots show navigation, content and signup controls clipped off-canvas.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the 1024 px minimum layout with intrinsic Grid/Flex sizing, clamp fluid dimensions, and verify every template at 320–412 px.

findings.summary: Reusable surfaces do not adapt at component level.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero @container rules while the same navigation, card and account components overflow in narrow containers.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reused components containment and apply size-aware container queries, with intrinsic fallback layout.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and target sizing are unreliable.
findings.evidence: Computed focus probes showed outline style none on search and Login; Lighthouse failed target-size, and the DOM probe found at least 30 interactive elements below 24 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge or space targets to at least 24 CSS px, preferably 44 px for primary touch actions.

findings.summary: The dark presentation is hard-coded rather than preference-driven.
findings.evidence: Default and prefers-color-scheme:dark screenshots are visually identical; under dark emulation computed colorScheme is normal and theme-color remains #ffffff.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark, supply preference-driven tokens, and keep theme-color synchronized for both schemes.

findings.summary: Animations continue under reduced-motion preference.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion:reduce active, getAnimations() still returned eight running animations, each with a 2000 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animation and transitions inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), preserving only necessary state feedback.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero view-transition rules on a multi-page experience with frequent route and modal state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation and same-document transitions for modal/state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 4615 px tall, but CSS inspection found no scroll timeline/state query and the captured chrome remains static.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware compact header without hiding core navigation.

findings.summary: A consent modal obscures the primary content on every sampled public page.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots show a large centered consent prompt covering cards, category navigation, video playback and signup before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the least interruptive consent surface allowed, keep essential content operable, and avoid re-prompting after an explicit choice.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is custom div chrome rather than a semantic modal primitive.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found one full-viewport overlay but zero dialog, role=dialog or popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the blocking consent surface with <dialog> and correct focus/inert handling, or use a non-modal disclosure where blocking is unnecessary.

findings.summary: The signup journey is not usable at the audited mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, the fixed desktop canvas leaves the signup card mostly off-screen; users see only a narrow clipped strip of the primary flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the responsive canvas fix to account routes and test email signup end-to-end at 320–412 px before release.

findings.summary: Synthetic mobile LCP misses the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 2.7 s and FCP 2.6 s on the homepage; the separate desktop trace measured LCP 1.62 s, so the mobile condition is the concern.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the first meaningful thumbnail/heading resources and reduce initial stylesheet/script contention; validate with field CWV after deployment.

findings.summary: Startup includes avoidable long main-thread tasks.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks, longest 160.84 ms, and 125.36 ms total blocking time; layout observation independently saw a 153 ms task.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up startup work, schedule non-critical work by priority, and defer recommendation/ad initialization until needed.

findings.summary: The initial dependency set is broad and includes blocking CSS.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 147 requests and 1.78 MB transferred; three parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets were confirmed as render-blocking candidates, alongside 66 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, and reduce the startup dependency tree while preserving cacheability.

findings.summary: JavaScript dominates initial transfer.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 1,017,548 transferred bytes to 66 scripts; index.js alone is 400,257 bytes and third-party Google code adds 98,484 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to remove unused code, split route-specific bundles, and load identity/recommendation dependencies only when their surface is invoked.

findings.summary: Some controls lack accessible names and one image lacks alt text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name on a visible control; the image audit found one missing alt among 36 images.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a stable accessible name and classify every image as meaningful alt text or decorative alt="".

findings.summary: Important text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.15:1 and 1.75:1 on the age-verification banner, 3.29:1 on view counts, and 3.29:1 on signup legal copy, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in default and forced-color modes, then rerun contrast checks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on core controls.
findings.evidence: Computed focus probes show outline none and no box-shadow on search and Login; several top navigation links also have outline style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring with adequate offset and verify a full keyboard walk in reading order.

findings.summary: Text and controls are clipped at narrow widths.
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshots cut off headings, banner copy, cards and the account panel because content remains 1024 px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow text containers to shrink and wrap intrinsically; avoid fixed widths and verify no clipping at zoom/reflow widths.

findings.summary: The experience fails reflow and includes undersized targets.
findings.evidence: At 360 CSS px, 664 px overflow remains and Lighthouse target-size fails; the viewport meta itself permits scaling, so layout is the blocker.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet WCAG reflow at 320 CSS px and increase target size/spacing without preventing zoom.

findings.summary: The conventional sitemap endpoint returns 404.
findings.evidence: robots.txt is valid and pages are indexable, but GET /sitemap.xml returned HTTP/2 404 with an empty body.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap index at the declared robots location (or clearly advertise the actual sitemap URLs) and keep canonical/robots signals consistent.

findings.summary: Video detail pages omit structured data.
findings.evidence: The representative detail page has accurate Open Graph tags but zero application/ld+json blocks, despite representing a VideoObject.
findings.suggestedFix: Add schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD matching the visible title, thumbnail, duration, upload date and access restrictions.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP transport protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS are present, but CSP only declares frame-ancestors; four of five cookies were flagged insecure and several use SameSite=None, including settings and g_state.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on all HTTPS cookies, use the strictest viable SameSite value, and deploy a nonce/hash-based script-src CSP in report-only mode before enforcement.

findings.summary: The pre-consent page has a large third-party/network footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 118 third-party requests transferring 1.59 MB across 11 third-party origins, including identity, recommendation and ad endpoints while the consent prompt was still open.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential third parties until consent, minimize recommendation payloads, and batch telemetry with documented retention and purpose.

findings.summary: Account creation exposes no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt fired on load, but signup offers Google, X and email/password; probes found no WebAuthn/passkey affordance or autocomplete=webauthn.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration/authentication and conditional UI alongside existing recovery options.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are weak or absent.
findings.evidence: Headers omit X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy; HSTS max-age is only 86400 seconds; Permissions-Policy only configures client hints and CSP lacks broader XSS directives.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff and a strict referrer policy, extend HSTS after readiness, restrict Permissions-Policy, and expand CSP with script/style/connect policies and Trusted Types where feasible.

findings.summary: CSS remains heavily dependent on physical left/right properties.
findings.evidence: The English page declares lang=en, but stylesheet inspection counted 684 physical left/right declarations versus 19 logical-property occurrences on a site linking dozens of languages including RTL locales.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate layout primitives to margin/padding/inset-inline and block/inline sizing; test Arabic, Persian and Hebrew routes with dir=rtl.

findings.summary: Rejecting optional cookies triggers a new accept-all prompt.
findings.evidence: After choosing Reject and opening email signup, the page displays “Some features may not be available… For a better user experience, please accept all cookies” with an Accept all cookies action.
findings.suggestedFix: Honor rejection without nagging; expose neutral preference management and explain only concrete feature dependencies at the point of use.

findings.summary: Signup validation messages are not exposed as live errors.
findings.evidence: Blank email submission shows “This field is required” and a password requirement, but the probe found no role=alert, aria-live or aria-invalid=true elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate errors with fields using aria-describedby/aria-invalid and announce the error summary in a polite live region after submission.

findings.summary: The email signup field disables autofill.
findings.evidence: The revealed signup form contains duplicate text inputs named email with autocomplete=off; password correctly uses new-password, but neither input has an associated label.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email and autocomplete=email, keep autocomplete=new-password, remove duplicate controls, and provide visible labels.

findings.summary: Account flow lacks a passkey option despite handling sensitive identity and age state.
findings.evidence: Signup clearly discloses public data use and offers reversible login navigation, but only federated and email/password enrollment are visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys, make account deletion/cancellation discoverable after signup, and retain the clear data-use disclosure.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 13 oversized images, 29 missing width/height attributes, 15 legacy-format URLs, and 8 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes, explicit dimensions and below-fold lazy loading.

findings.summary: Recommendation and advertising work starts broadly on initial load.
findings.evidence: The initial HAR contains 147 requests, 66 scripts and long recommendation/ad requests around 2.4–2.8 s, before the user has selected content.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize or defer recommendations, identity and ads until consent/intent, and cancel work when hidden or irrelevant.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes most initial network bytes.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 1,588,914 of 1,781,408 transferred bytes (89%) and 118 of 147 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, gate optional integrations, and load media/ad code only near interaction.
